brdf_lommel_seeliger — 3D render op

• Data kinds: normalmap → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.brdf_lommel_seeliger(normals, light=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), view=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), w: 'float' = 0.42) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import render_shade; render_shade.brdf_lommel_seeliger(normals, light=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), view=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), w: 'float' = 0.42) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, ops3d.get("brdf_lommel_seeliger"))

Usage

Shade a normal map with the Lommel-Seeliger reflectance law (regolith that stays bright to the limb) and return I/F (H, W).

Lambert (the diffuse term of phong_shade) goes to 0 at the limb (μ→0), but Lommel-Seeliger is μ0/(μ0+μ), so it stays bright at μ0 even at the limb, giving the "flat disc" look of asteroids and the Moon. w = single-scattering albedo. fail-closed (normal shape, range of w).

The computation is identical to model='lommel_seeliger' of brdf_shade: for each pixel it takes μ0 = clip(N·L, 0, 1) and μ = clip(N·V, 0, 1), and returns I/F = π · (w/4π) · μ0/(μ0+μ) (= (w/4)·μ0/(μ0+μ)). Pixels where μ0 or μ is 0 or less (faces not lit, faces turned away from the line of sight) are 0.

• normals: float (H, W, 3). Vectors of length 0 are treated as background and give output 0 (the normals of render3d.render_mesh can be passed as is). Normalisation is done internally.

• light / view: direction vectors pointing surface→light source and surface→viewpoint (normalised internally). The camera looks along -Z by convention, so the default is view=(0,0,1). Parallel-light, orthographic approximation; the directions are constant across the image.

• w: single-scattering albedo; anything outside (0, 1] raises ValueError.

Returns the I/F as float64 (H, W). With orthographic projection and light == view (phase angle 0), μ0 = μ and the whole foreground takes the uniform value w/8. Values lie in [0, w/4) and are not normalised to [0,1]. For highlights use phong_shade; to include the opposition effect and roughness use brdf_hapke.
